Why DIRECT rather than ADAPTIVE: "new subsystem" normally routes M→A→L→C→E→H, but this subject carries one unambiguous gate question — a speculative abstraction with a stated absence of demand ("nobody has asked for another"). M is a blocking stage; A/L/C/E/H stay unloaded until it passes.

## What I found

A plugin registry for third-party output formats, assessed at the Minimum gate against the actual tree (all five files in `src/`). The answer is don't build it — the record calls this **DROP**, on a necessity failure rather than a cost complaint. The fact that decided it: there is exactly one formatter (`src/format/json.js:1`, a one-line `JSON.stringify` wrapper), all three commands call it directly, and no second format is named or requested. `package.json:5` is `"private": true`, so the actor the design serves — a third party authoring a format — has no way to obtain or extend this CLI today.

## Why it matters

Building it ships a public extension contract (the thing you can least cheaply change) for zero current consumers; every later change to how a command produces text then has to preserve a plugin API nobody is using. Not building it costs you roughly five lines of work later: when a second format is actually requested, `src/cli.js` already parses argv and is the one place a `--format` switch belongs.

Separately, the proposal confuses an aspect with a subsystem. "Output format" is one obligation (serialize a value to text) with one mechanism (`toJson`). Modeling it as a module that sits between commands and formatters adds an indirection level and three dependency edges while removing none — the three commands pass differently shaped data (`{records}` wrapper, aggregate, pass-through), so there is no shared seam for a registry to own.

## Do this first

1. Record the rejection and stop — no code change. Per `zero-copy-requirements`, that decision belongs in an issue, not in a doc in the repo; the code already says what it does.
2. If a second format is requested: add `src/format/<name>.js` and resolve a two-entry map from a `--format` flag in `src/cli.js:6-9`. No new subsystem.
3. Reopen the registry question only when formatters must ship from *outside* this repo — which requires dropping `private: true` and publishing, i.e. a distribution decision, not a design one.

## What I did not check

- Gates A/L/C/E/H never loaded: M is a blocking stage and returned DROP, so placement, complexity, enforcement, and shift-left have no candidate to judge. Closes with `/alchemy A` (or a fuller pass) *after* a real second-format requirement exists.
- Runtime behavior: `node src/cli.js report <file>` not run. The finding is structural (call graph across the whole of `src/`), so it does not depend on execution.
- Demand outside this repo: no git history (not a repository) and no telemetry. Your statement that nobody has asked is the only evidence on value; a roadmap item I can't see would change the `Revisit when` trigger, not the verdict.
